risk_reasons: Schema migration applied to both Supabase projects in lockstep (staging first), which .claude/CLAUDE.md classifies as high risk.
job_outbox is the transactional outbox dispatch spine (invariant #2). A wrong RLS posture (FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY) would lock out the owner-role worker and stop every async job in the platform.
The change closes a live authorization gap: on staging the public anon key currently holds INSERT on job_outbox with RLS off, so a stranger can enqueue jobs the OutboxPoller dispatches.
goal: job_outbox carries deny-all RLS and zero anon/authenticated privileges on production, staging, and the local test database, so the three environments are in lockstep and the staging anon key can neither read nor enqueue outbox jobs.
non_goals: Do not add any RLS policy. Deny-all means zero policies, the poller_heartbeats (118) and auto_approval_policies posture.
Do not set FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. The worker reaches job_outbox as the table owner, which bypasses RLS only while FORCE is off.

Do not change ci:rls-audit, ci:tenant-scope, TENANT_TABLES, REVIEWED_NOT_TENANT_SCOPED, or docs/security/rls-inventory.md. Owner decision 2026-09-07: future tables state their RLS posture in their own migration instead.
Do not REVOKE anon/authenticated on any other deny-all table. That is a separate reviewed change.
Do not change outbox enqueue, dispatch, claim, or status behavior. No TypeScript production code changes.
Do not disable RLS on production job_outbox. Convergence is upward, toward the stricter posture.
user_visible_behavior: Operational: a PostgREST request to /rest/v1/job_outbox carrying the staging anon or authenticated key returns a permission error instead of outbox rows, and an INSERT through that key is refused.
Operational: worker outbox dispatch is unchanged in every environment. OutboxPoller throughput, claim behavior, and job_outbox writes from postgres.js transactions all behave exactly as before.
Developer: after this migration lands, pnpm test:db:setup must be re-run before ci:rls-audit and the live-DB suites pass locally.
invariants: Invariant #2 holds: state change plus job_outbox row stay in one Postgres transaction, and the OutboxPoller keeps dispatching them.
job_outbox.relrowsecurity is true and job_outbox.relforcerowsecurity is false in all three environments.
job_outbox has zero rows in pg_policies.
anon and authenticated hold no privilege on job_outbox.
postgres (table owner) and service_role privileges on job_outbox are unchanged.
No code path reaches job_outbox through supabase-js. Verified 2026-09-07: rg found zero matches for from('job_outbox') in src and worker.
edge_cases: Production already has relrowsecurity=true, so ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is a no-op there and does not error. Verified by introspection 2026-09-07.
Production still carries anon/authenticated grants, so the REVOKE is a real production change, not a no-op. It is a tightening and no code path uses those roles on this table.
Staging and the local test database have relrowsecurity=false, so the ALTER is the substantive statement there.
REVOKE ALL names anon and authenticated only. service_role carries BYPASSRLS and postgres owns the table, so neither is touched.
The migration is immutable once applied. migration-immutability-guard.sh blocks edits at or below the recorded head, so any correction is migration 120.
The Supabase migration ledger does not track RepWorth's 0xx migrations. Application is proven by schema introspection only.

rollback_plan: The migration is not auto-reversible; an applied migration is immutable. To undo, write migration 120 with ALTER TABLE job_outbox DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON job_outbox TO anon, authenticated, and apply it staging first. Rollback is only warranted if worker dispatch stops, which would mean the owner-role assumption is wrong. The staging ride is the detector: if staging dispatch keeps working after apply, production is safe, because production has already run with RLS enabled since 2026-04-05.
observability: OutboxPoller dispatch continues on the staging Railway worker after apply. Confirmed from the worker logs and from a non-zero dispatched count in job_outbox.
